answer: One defense is a stake that melts slowly, like a glacier: every agent identity must lock real value for weeks, refunded only after verified honest work. Spawning thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of locked stakes, pricing the attack out. Identities are also grouped into small trust islands that vouch for their members and lose reputation as a whole if one member cheats, so an attacker must corrupt an entire island rather than mint one account. Each attestation is signed with a per-agent cipher key tied to the stake, so fakes cannot forge each other's history.
